claims.text:
18. k-means-forced-k

Target / packet: ai-k-means-forced-k · C1. Prerequisites: ai:k-means-clustering, probability:clustering-illusion.

Nearest / distinct payoff: k-means-clustering → bad-start-kmeans. A requested k can split a uniformly spaced finite cloud with no special gap between groups; smaller within-cluster error alone cannot identify a true population count.

Finite primary model: Uniformly spaced finite points [0,1,2,3,4,5]. Declared centroid partitions for k=2: centers 1,4 give groups [0,1,2]/[3,4,5], SSE 4. For k=3 centers.5,2.5,4.5 give pairs and SSE 1.5.

Countercase and mathematical boundary: Both partitions are self-consistent nearest-centroid solutions, yet data have equal adjacent gaps: requested k creates groups without proving distinct populations. No statistical claim that continuous real data have no clusters.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict whether k=3 still returns groups; recall why reduced SSE alone cannot establish a true population count.

Required observable evidence: Show actual assignment and centroid recomputation, with no gap fabricated between points.

Source obligation: [scikit-learn clustering documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html), acquired method body §§2.3.2 k-means,2.3.6 hierarchical methods,2.3.7 DBSCAN. Each local convention and actual result is independently derivable; do not infer true populations from requested groups.
 Shipped local model and displayed expression addresses: model.ts compute; Demo.tsx Figure; Stage retained computed witnesses.
